selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the speaker call his own nafs at the start?
questions.answer: Foolish.

questions.question: Why are those examples important?
questions.answer: They show that carrying something good is not the same as creating it.

questions.question: Do those examples teach that the seed and branch are fully in charge?
questions.answer: No, they do not.

questions.question: What does pride do to blessings, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It lowers their value.

questions.question: Name one thing the nafs should do with blessings.
questions.answer: Thank Allah.

questions.question: Which is the better quality: fame or humility?
questions.answer: Humility.

questions.question: What is the nafs compared to in the world?
questions.answer: Nature.

questions.question: Why are ugly-looking things sometimes linked to them?
questions.answer: So Allah is known to be perfect and free of defect.

questions.question: What is so bad about acting like a partner with the Creator?
questions.answer: It is a huge wrong and great foolishness.

questions.question: Why should the nafs not say, “I was chosen, so I must be better”?
questions.answer: Because those gifts were given to it out of need, weakness, and poverty before Allah.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in this passage?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own nafs.

questions.question: What first nature example is used to explain the lesson?
questions.answer: A tiny seed connected to a tree full of figs.

questions.question: Why is that thought corrected right away?
questions.answer: Because the nafs does not truly make those blessings.

questions.question: How does conceit affect blessings?
questions.answer: It ruins them.

questions.question: What should come from a believer after receiving blessings?
questions.answer: Thanks to Allah.

questions.question: What action should replace the wish for people’s praise?
questions.answer: Seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: What do the nafs and nature have in common?
questions.answer: They receive good but are where evil is linked.

questions.question: Why were they made as a kind of cover?
questions.answer: To carry the blame for what seems ugly, while Allah is above all fault.

questions.question: What judgment is given about worshiping oneself or nature?
questions.answer: It is foolish and a great injustice.

questions.question: What main warning does this passage give about the nafs?
questions.answer: Do not let it become proud and steal credit from Allah.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly correcting in the nafs?
questions.answer: Its pride and self-love.

questions.question: What tree fruit is used as an example?
questions.answer: Figs.

questions.question: Why is the nafs told it should not be proud of blessings?
questions.answer: Because it is not the real maker of them.

questions.question: What happens to blessings when a person is thankful or unthankful?
questions.answer: Thankfulness keeps them right, but unthankfulness cancels them.

title: Title and 1 Point Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self
